To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new tomato introgression population is described that is complementary to the widely used S. pennelli introgression lines, that this new resource can be used for rapid trait mapping and that it can be used for fine-mapping of metabolic quantitative trait loci.

we have developed a resource of 107 introgression lines derived from a cross between Solanum neoricci and cultivated tomato, and we have demonstrated their utility for fine mapping of quantitative trait loci.

the S.  neorickii B.ILs represent a powerful resource that complements the S. pennellii B.IL population, and that the S. neorickii lines can be used to map and fine-map genes underlying quantitative traits in tomato.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new resource for tomato quantitative trait locus mapping, and we demonstrate its power by using metabolic profiling and candidate gene validation.
the identification of the genetic basis of quantitative traits in tomato.
the development of a new resource for fine-scale mapping and validation of quantitative trait loci in tomato.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the S. Neorickii B.I.Ls are a very powerful resource to complement the S. pennisii population and that the use of these resources will facilitate the identification of the genetic basis of complex quantitative traits in tomato and will contribute to the understanding of the evolution of tomato.
the S.  neorickii B.ILs are a powerful and complementary resource to the S.  pennellii resources for trait fine-maping in tomato.

the BILs derived from the cross between S. neorrickii and S. lycopersicum are a complementary and valuable resource that can be used in conjunction with the S. pennisellii resources for trait mapping and fine mapping in tomato.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S.  neorickii BILI population is a valuable resource to complement the S. pennellii resources for tomato quantitative genetics.
the S. Neorickii B.ILs represent a powerful complement to S. pennelli BILs, and the data generated from this work are freely available to the research community at http://www.solgenomics.net.
this resource is a valuable complement to the S. pennisellii resource for trait mapping in tomato.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a second wild tomato species as an introgression population provides a complementary and powerful tool for fine-mapping in the tomato genome, and that the S.  neorickii B ILs are a useful resource for this purpose.

the S. Neorickii introgressions are an important complement to the existing S. pennelli resource, and we expect this resource to be used extensively by the tomato community in the future.
